bullets.title: FOXA: Wolfe upgrades to Outperform, $71 PT on Roku deal re-rating
bullets.body: Wolfe upgrades FOXA to Outperform with $71 PT (36% upside) after shares fell 17% on the $22B Roku deal announcement and now sit 23% below pre-deal levels. The deal doubles Fox's long-term sales CAGR, lifts streaming to ~45% of TV engagement, and targets $400M in cost synergies; pro forma trades at 11.8x NTM UFCF. SOTP analysis implies $80/share fair value.

bullets.title: CRM, NOW: Guggenheim upgrades both to Buy on AI fears 'priced in'
bullets.body: Guggenheim upgraded CRM to Buy at $228 PT and NOW to Buy at $125 PT, arguing current valuations imply decline into perpetuity that Guggenheim views as excessive. Firm expects subscription revenue growth to stabilize in 2026 and potentially accelerate into 2027 despite material but manageable AI disruption risk; NOW upgrade also tied to expected improvement in federal business.

bullets.title: AFRM: Citi reiterates Buy, raises PT to $115 on FY27 29%+ GMV conviction
bullets.body: Citi raises AFRM PT from $100 to $115, citing achievable FY27 GMV growth of 29%+ (above management's 25%+ target) and FY29 GAAP EPS potential of $5.00 vs. consensus $3.70. The note reflects high conviction on growth/profitability trajectory.

bullets.title: META: 'Meta Compute' cloud launch — mixed read on AI capex discipline
bullets.body: Meta is building a cloud business ('Meta Compute') to sell excess AI computing capacity, potentially generating $10-15B annually and adding ~8% to 2028 EPS as a 'backup safety valve.' Citi notes early feedback is split — bulls see monetization supporting further AI investment; bears read excess capacity as evidence of overbuilding.

bullets.title: BE: Bloom Energy surges ~7.5% on Brookfield partnership expansion to $25B
bullets.body: Bloom Energy expanded its AI infrastructure partnership with Brookfield from $5B to $25B (25 GW capacity framework), with ~2.5 GW already signed (AEP, ORCL, NBIS) and a path to 5 GW+ by 2030. Stock was up ~7.5% premarket on the news; MS views this as strong signal of hyperscaler onsite power demand.

bullets.title: OKLO: DOE approves final safety analysis for Grove reactor; first criticality targeted July 2026
bullets.body: Oklo received DOE approval for the final safety analysis of its Grove Isotope Test Reactor in Texas, with first criticality targeted for July 2026. Stock up ~3.4-3.9% premarket on the news.

bullets.title: MRVL: Meta's in-house Vistara CXL ASIC is an incremental negative, but thesis intact
bullets.body: Hedgeye flags Meta's custom Vistara CXL ASIC (DDR4 reuse) as an incremental negative for Marvell's Structera X product but says Marvell's broader CXL portfolio and hyperscaler adoption thesis remain intact. MRVL was down ~2.1% premarket in the broad semiconductor selloff.

bullets.title: Semis under pressure: MU, AMD, SNDK, GLW all lower; DRAM 70 and NVDA 190 key levels
bullets.body: Morning market color flags a rotation out of momentum/semis with DRAM below 70 described as 'concerning' — needs to reclaim that level to restore confidence. Critical technical levels cited: DRAM 70, SMH 575, SPX 7380, NVDA 190. Premarket: SNDK -4.7%, GLW -3.8%, MU -3.3%, AMD -1.4%; correlation indicator at 5-yr lows historically precedes 10-20% momentum corrections.

bullets.title: GOOGL: AI Overviews cutting outbound clicks 40%, raising monetization risk
bullets.body: Citi cites study showing GOOGL's AI Overviews reduce outbound organic clicks by 39.8% and increase zero-click searches by 34.5% without improving user experience, posing a structural risk to the web traffic ecosystem. Separately, GOOGL faces a Swedish court-ordered $1.5B antitrust payment to Klarna and a South Korea app store review.

bullets.title: MSFT: Layoffs <2.5% of workforce next week; Kyndryl sovereignty partnership minor positive
bullets.body: MSFT is planning job cuts affecting less than 2.5% of its workforce next week in sales, consulting, and Xbox divisions; stock was up ~1.8% premarket, suggesting market sees cuts as cost discipline. Separately, Kyndryl expanded a sovereignty cloud partnership with MSFT targeting data-residency-sensitive enterprise customers.

bullets.title: AAPL: Reducing iPhone 17 production plans on lower shipment forecasts
bullets.body: Apple is said to be cutting production plans for the iPhone 17 lineup amid lower shipment forecasts, per MacRumors. No quantification provided, but directionally negative for the supply chain.

bullets.title: AMZN: Best-in-class agentic commerce at 77% rec rate; expanding Alexa price-history features
bullets.body: DA Davidson's agentic commerce testing showed AMZN with a 77% recommendation rate across 35 project-based queries — best-in-class — well ahead of peers. AMZN is also expanding Alexa for Shopping with 30/90/365-day price history to support AI-assisted purchasing, leaning into the agentic retail shift.

bullets.title: MU: Strategic Customer Agreement with GM; stock weak on memory sector selloff
bullets.body: Micron signed a Strategic Customer Agreement with GM for long-term supply of memory and storage for vehicle production — one of 16 SCAs discussed on its FQ3 earnings call. Despite this positive, MU was down ~3.3% premarket as the broader memory sector sold off (DRAM below key 70 support level).

bullets.title: JPM technical note: Hyperscaler-semi divergence mirrors 1999-2000; monitor GOOGL, AMZN, MSFT, META, ORCL
bullets.body: JPM's equity technical team warns that hyperscalers (GOOGL, AMZN, MSFT, META, ORCL) are underperforming semiconductors, creating a divergence similar to the 1999-2000 Communications Services vs. Equipment split. Summer hyperscaler weakness could trigger a sentiment-driven fall selloff; S&P support at 7000-7200 seen as buying opportunity if distribution doesn't form by Labor Day.

bullets.title: FOXA/ROKU, CMCSA: Media-specific catalysts — Fox upgrade, Comcast spinoff regulatory review
bullets.body: Beyond the Wolfe FOXA upgrade (see above), Wolfe Research hosted a replay Q&A with ex-FCC counsel on Comcast's plan to spin out NBCU and Sky, examining the regulatory approval pathway and potential M&A consequences. No rating action on CMCSA disclosed.

bullets.title: GS Conviction List adds AVGO-adjacent AI capex theme; 2Q earnings seen +22% YoY
bullets.body: Goldman's July conviction list adds EL, NXT, and WFC; separately, GS notes June S&P pullback masked semi outperformance despite Mag-7 declining ~7%, and views hyperscaler capex expectations as still too conservative. 2Q S&P earnings expected to grow +22% YoY with AI investment as primary driver; market broadening creates alpha opportunities.

bullets.title: DKNG: Q2 EBITDA estimates in low $100Ms; hold% trends reversed despite World Cup
bullets.body: Hedgeye warns DKNG and FLUT Q2 EBITDA estimates sit in the low $100Ms, with hold percentage trends reversing negatively in May despite World Cup tailwinds. Kalshi's sports handle up 7% W/W with ~26.6% market share, driven by World Cup at ~67% of handle.

bullets.title: CEG, VST, TLN: Power stocks mixed — PJM regulatory uncertainty weighing on IPPs
bullets.body: IPP stocks (CEG, VST, TLN) traded off on PJM reliability backstop mechanism uncertainty and curtailment program discussions, with Board submission to FERC expected July 10. PJM separately advanced a new capacity procurement plan driven by data center demand surge; CEG down 3.5% on the day and 25.8% from 52-week high.

bullets.title: SHOP: UBS payments dinner highlights long-term monetization opportunity
bullets.body: UBS is hosting a Shopify investor lunch in Boston on July 15 alongside a broader payments dinner covering Shopify's long-term growth algorithm, enterprise opportunity, and payments monetization as part of a deep-dive on the PayFac-as-a-Service convergence trend. No rating action disclosed but signals active UBS engagement on SHOP positioning.

bullets.title: NVDA, FN, COHR: Roth survey probes GPU cluster optical transceiver sourcing dynamics
bullets.body: Roth's Vol. 6 GPU cluster survey examines whether hyperscalers/CSPs are buying 800G/1.6T optical transceivers directly from NVDA (Innolight/Coherent resale) vs. sourcing from Fabrinet, assessing switching likelihood and premium pricing expectations. Results pending but directionally relevant for FN and COHR positioning around the AI infrastructure buildout.
